prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1271; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured's agent reporting a side impact at a controlled intersection, with the claimant's vehicle struck on the driver's side. The claimant has retained counsel, and all contact will be routed through the attorney's office going forward.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant's vehicle at the scene and lists the other driver as cited for failing to yield. Confirmed the claimant was present in the vehicle at the time of the collision.

Entry 3: Photos submitted by the insured show the impact area and confirm several of the damage details described in the initial report. No independent witnesses have come forward to date.

Entry 4: Inspected the vehicle with the repair estimator. The damage is largely consistent with the described impact direction and angle. Nothing in the inspection suggests prior damage to the same panels, and no earlier repairs were found on record.

Entry 5: Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy and that coverage was active on the date of loss. Found nothing indicating the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 6: Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness following the collision and has been seen by a treating physician. The reported injury fits well with the force and type of impact shown in the photos and the estimate.

Entry 7: Medical records reviewed. Claimant has a past history of a minor strain in the same region several years ago, which resolved fully with no lasting limitation noted in the file.

Entry 8: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for a cervical strain of this kind. Requested updated treatment notes and therapy attendance records from the provider through counsel.

Entry 9: Spoke with the claimant on two occasions. The account of how the collision happened has stayed the same in each conversation, with no material differences in sequence or description.

Entry 10: Received the requested treatment records and the repair estimate. Reviewed both against the police report and photos and noted the findings for the file. Medical bills are being reviewed for reasonableness.

Entry 11: File remains open pending receipt of the final treatment summary and the attorney's settlement demand. Next review scheduled once those documents are received.
